lesson: Today, we work on one technique. It is starting a poem in the middle of something, with no introduction, no names, no setup. The poem just begins as if you walked in partway through. This poem does that. It opens with, the fog came down in the night like a wet sheet. No greeting, no explanation of where you are. Then lies now in the low field. And later, down in the shed, the jars sit half filled and waiting. You are dropped into a scene already going. It works because your mind fills the gaps. You did not get told where you are, so you pay attention and piece it together. That keeps you leaning in. Try this. Cut your first two sentences of.
